theory.reason: Nora saw Quill control the trumpet when Gideon's voice sounded. She treats the performance as Quill's doing and mistakes the fraud for the murder. The cylinder does not tell her who killed Gideon.

suspects.name: Clara Hensley
suspects.role: Gideon March's secretary and research assistant
suspects.public_hook: Gideon's secretary is sorting his notes into neat piles beside the room where he died.
suspects.secret: She leaked selected confidential research to Lenora Quill, killed Gideon when he confronted her, and substituted cylinder 43 into Quill's apparatus.

suspects.name: Lenora Quill
suspects.public_hook: The medium held the brass trumpet when Gideon's voice came through it, and her hand shook afterward.
suspects.secret: Her séances are fraudulent; she uses a concealed playback/acoustic route and receives private client information in advance.

suspects.name: Edwin Rusk
suspects.public_hook: The Larkspur's owner left the séance just after Gideon's voice came through Quill's trumpet.
suspects.secret: He profits from Quill's séances, allowed the service modifications, found cylinder 43 after the séance, and locked it away to protect the hotel.

suspects.name: Beatrice Ashcombe
suspects.public_hook: The séance patron looks toward the writing room when Gideon is mentioned.
suspects.secret: She supplied Quill private letters, threatened Gideon over material he planned to publish, and secretly overheard part of Gideon's confrontation with Clara.

canonical_timeline.event: Gideon records cylinder 43, including the phrase he intends to use to expose Quill's direct-voice trick.
Clara transcribes Gideon's working notes and knows what cylinder 43 contains.
Gideon confronts Clara in the writing room after tracing leaked confidential research to Quill.
Clara kills Gideon with a heavy brass bookend during the confrontation.
Clara takes cylinder 43 and substitutes it into Quill's concealed séance apparatus.
Clara rejoins the gathering and remains visibly present.
Quill unknowingly triggers cylinder 43 at her planned direct-voice cue; Gideon's prerecorded voice is heard.
Quill and Rusk inspect the apparatus; Rusk finds cylinder 43.
Rusk locks cylinder 43 in the hotel strongbox to hide the fraud.
Rusk knocks at Gideon's writing-room door; the body is discovered.

essential_truths.text: The later voice attributed to Gideon was a prerecorded cylinder played through Quill's fraudulent apparatus.
Gideon was killed before the séance voice was heard.
Clara had been feeding Gideon's confidential research into Quill's performances, and Gideon discovered it.
Clara killed Gideon and used her access to his recording and Quill's fraud to stage the later-alive impression.

opening_opportunities.label: Gideon's Things
opening_opportunities.description: Go through the work he left behind.

opening_opportunities.label: The Séance Room
opening_opportunities.description: Inspect the room where everyone heard him alive.

opening_opportunities.label: Question Someone
opening_opportunities.description: Talk to Clara, Quill, Rusk, or Beatrice.

writing-room.scene: Gideon's chair lies on its side beside the writing desk. A heavy brass bookend has been set back crookedly, leaving a clean rectangle in the dust beneath it. A fresh carbon sheet in the wastebasket carries one incomplete typed line: 'After Quill, Hensley.'

discoveries.label: Displaced bookend
discoveries.fact: A heavy brass bookend was moved and replaced recently.

discoveries.label: Gideon's unfinished note
discoveries.fact: Gideon's last typed line reads: 'After Quill, Hensley.'

gideon-materials.scene: Gideon numbered his dictation cylinders like a man who expected future historians to be grateful. The rack jumps from 42 to 44. His transcript folder still contains page 43, including a peculiar sentence: 'Mrs. Quill, do carry on. I can hear every word.' Clara Hensley's transcription initials appear at the foot of that page.

discoveries.label: Missing cylinder 43
discoveries.fact: Gideon's numbered rack is missing cylinder 43.

discoveries.label: Transcript of cylinder 43
discoveries.fact: Before the séance, Gideon recorded the exact unusual sentence later heard through Quill's trumpet.

discoveries.label: Clara's transcription initials
discoveries.fact: The transcript of cylinder 43 bears Clara Hensley's transcription initials.

seance-room.scene: The trumpet sits on the séance table, but its base is wrong for an ornament: a narrow coupling disappears through the table pedestal toward the old service wall. Quill's cue sheet lists a bell, a whisper, and 'Ashcombe voice.' Gideon March is nowhere on it.

discoveries.label: Concealed voice route
discoveries.fact: The séance trumpet connects to a concealed service-side playback/acoustic route.

discoveries.label: Quill's cue sheet
discoveries.fact: Quill's planned effects did not include Gideon's voice.

clara-hensley.opening: Clara folds Gideon's loose notes into three exact piles. 'I transcribed cylinder 43 at 11:23, five minutes after Gideon recorded it.' She squares the pages against the table edge.
clara-hensley.claim: 'I last saw Gideon shortly after eleven twenty. I did not go back to the writing-room corridor before they found him.'

discoveries.label: Clara's timeline
discoveries.fact: Clara claims she did not go near the writing room after about 11:20 PM.

discoveries.label: Clara knew cylinder 43
discoveries.fact: Clara acknowledges she transcribed cylinder 43 earlier that evening.

follow_thread.prompt: Ask Clara about Gideon's unfinished note.
follow_thread.scene: Clara reads 'After Quill, Hensley' once, then sets the page down. 'Gideon liked to show people how much he knew.' She aligns its edge with the others. She will not say how Quill obtained material from Gideon's private files.

discovery.label: Clara avoids the source question
discovery.fact: Clara will not explain how Quill obtained information found in Gideon's private research.

lenora-quill.opening: Quill has removed one glove. Her bare hand shakes as she folds it. 'The audience heard Mr. March. I cannot tell you why he chose my room.'
lenora-quill.claim: 'The trumpet carried a spirit voice. I never receive information before a sitting.'

discoveries.label: Quill denies advance information
discoveries.fact: Quill denies receiving private information before séances.

conditional.prompt: Ask Quill to account for the voice from her trumpet.
conditional.scene: Quill sets the glove on the table. 'It is a tube, a cabinet, and a cue I have used for years. Gideon's voice was not mine. I thought he had found the service cupboard and turned the trick on me.' Without the audience, she speaks plainly.

discoveries.label: Quill admits the fraud
discoveries.fact: Quill admits the trumpet uses a concealed apparatus and says Gideon's voice was not part of her planned performance.

follow_thread.prompt: Ask Quill who gave her information before the sitting.
follow_thread.scene: Quill closes her case before she answers. 'Miss Hensley brought envelopes. I paid her for them.' She takes out a folded receipt. Clara Hensley's initials sit beside two cash payments. 'If this reaches the guests, the sittings are finished.'

discovery.label: Payments tied to Clara
discovery.fact: Quill's private records show cash payments associated with Clara Hensley.

edwin-rusk.opening: Rusk straightens a chair that no one has asked him to move. 'There are guests upstairs. I need this corridor cleared before they come down.'
edwin-rusk.claim: 'I knew nothing about Quill's equipment. After the voice, I did not touch the séance apparatus.'

discoveries.label: Rusk denies touching the apparatus
discoveries.fact: Rusk claims he never inspected or handled Quill's equipment after Gideon's voice was heard.

conditional.prompt: Ask Rusk what he did after Gideon's voice.
conditional.scene: Rusk grips the chair back. 'I checked the service side. Before the sitting, I saw Clara come out of the writing-room passage and return to the guests. After March's voice, Quill and I opened the cabinet. We found one of his cylinders where hers should have been. I put it in the strongbox.' He looks toward the occupied rooms upstairs. 'If the fraud ruins this hotel, I lose the business.'

discoveries.label: Rusk found Gideon's cylinder
discoveries.fact: Rusk found a Gideon March cylinder in Quill's apparatus after the séance voice.

discoveries.label: Rusk saw Clara return
discoveries.fact: Before the séance voice, Rusk saw Clara leave the writing-room passage and return to the gathering.

follow_thread.prompt: Ask Rusk who could enter the service corridor.
follow_thread.scene: Rusk names Quill, himself, two hotel employees, and then reluctantly Clara. 'Miss Hensley came through the service corridor more than once. I assumed she was arranging March's little war.'

discovery.label: Clara knew the service route
discovery.fact: Rusk confirms Clara had used the service corridor associated with Quill's apparatus before the murder.

beatrice-ashcombe.opening: Beatrice looks toward the writing room. 'If you mean to ask whether I threatened Gideon, be specific. I threatened him twice.' She admits giving Quill letters and objects before the sitting, though she denied it before the other guests.
beatrice-ashcombe.claim: 'Gideon meant to publish material about my late husband's finances. We argued. I saw nothing useful near his room.'

discoveries.label: Beatrice threatened Gideon
discoveries.fact: Beatrice threatened Gideon earlier in the evening over material he intended to publish.

discoveries.label: Beatrice supplied Quill letters
discoveries.fact: Beatrice privately gave Quill letters and objects before the séance despite publicly denying advance contact.

conditional.prompt: Ask Beatrice what she meant by seeing nothing useful near Gideon's room.
conditional.scene: Beatrice looks toward the door. 'I said I saw nothing useful. I was at his door. I had threatened him already, and I would not explain why I was there.' She sets down her glass. 'I heard Gideon say, ‘You sold my work to a parlour trick.’ Clara answered. Then I heard a heavy impact. I did not see the blow. I saw Clara leave the corridor. Later she was seated with us when his voice came through.'

discoveries.label: Argument and impact
discoveries.fact: Before the séance voice, Beatrice heard Gideon accuse someone of selling his work, heard Clara answer, and then heard a heavy impact.

discoveries.label: Beatrice saw Clara leave
discoveries.fact: Beatrice saw Clara leave the writing-room corridor before Clara later appeared at the séance.

discoveries.label: Clara was present for the voice
discoveries.fact: Clara was visibly present with the group when Gideon's voice came through the trumpet.

follow_thread.prompt: Ask Beatrice what her letters did and did not tell Quill.
follow_thread.scene: The letters explain most of Quill's performance, but not one odd reference to a sealed family account Gideon had uncovered separately. The same phrase appears in Gideon's private research notes, in a section Clara transcribed.

discovery.label: Private detail crossed from Gideon's file
discovery.fact: A distinctive detail used by Quill appears in Gideon's private research but not in Beatrice's supplied letters; Clara transcribed the relevant section.

competition.title: The Locked Box
competition.research_abstraction: The solo fixture represents a contested lock with a human lock-picking interaction and a deterministic authored rival clock. It does not validate production simultaneous-picking support.

fallback_public_observation.label: Cylinder 43
fallback_public_observation.fact: Cylinder 43 contains Gideon speaking the exact sentence later heard through Quill's trumpet.

winner_private_observation.label: Cylinder 43
winner_private_observation.fact: Cylinder 43 contains Gideon speaking the exact sentence later heard through Quill's trumpet.

effects.label: Listen In
effects.description: Copy the rival's private observation from the locked box.

effects.label: Follow the Thread
effects.description: Take one contextual follow-up with a person you have interviewed before entering Last Call.

case_file.instructions: Choose your culprit, then select four or five facts that best reconstruct what happened.
